title: Diagnostic Gateway
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Complete the Value Builder diagnostic so Trinity can generate your report, recommendations, and a personalised starting point and module path.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: Gather key financial and operational documents

title: Financial Management
focus: Financial clarity, cost and margin performance, and a reporting rhythm the owner will actually maintain.
purpose: V1 establishes the financial foundation for every other module. The owner gains a clear, plain-language understanding of how the business performs, where money is being lost through cost structure and slow invoicing, and what to watch month to month. Almost every other module depends on the outputs produced here. This module is about commercial clarity, not accounting technicalities.
core_outcomes: The owner can explain their financial position in simple terms.
Major expense lines are reviewed and cost adjustments identified.
The invoicing process is reviewed and cash-timing improvements agreed.
Margin leaks are identified and a small number of high-impact actions are agreed.
A lightweight financial reporting rhythm is in place and owned.

required_inputs.label: Diagnostic report, V1 module assessment
Profit and loss, 3 years
Balance sheet, current and prior
Revenue breakdown by product, service or segment
Aged receivables and current payment terms
Accountant and bookkeeper contact details
Existing budget or forecast, where one exists

preparation_summary.duration: 60 to 120 minutes depending on data quality

preparation_checklist.text: Load financial data into Trinity and generate the Financial Health Summary.
Review margin trends, revenue mix, labour and subcontractor ratios, overhead patterns.
Identify the largest expense lines and those that have grown fastest over the period.
Review the debtor position, average days to payment, and any work sitting uninvoiced.
Identify red flags: chronic low margin, structural under-pricing, excessive rework, negative equity, director loans, contingent liabilities.
Note 3 to 5 suspected improvement levers to test in the session.
Where the diagnostic returned "not sure" responses, list them for direct verification with the bookkeeper or accountant. Do not assume they are in order.

agenda.title: Frame the session
agenda.detail: Clarify that the advisor is not the accountant or bookkeeper. Position the session as improving profitability, improving decision-making, and reducing financial stress.

agenda.title: Review the Financial Health Summary
agenda.detail: Present in plain language: gross margin, net margin, revenue trend, major cost drivers. Check understanding continuously. Avoid jargon.

agenda.title: Expenses review and adjustment
agenda.detail: Work through the major expense lines and test whether each still earns its place. Cover the three biggest costs, what has grown fastest, which costs are fixed versus flexible, and whether personal expenses are running through the business and properly separated.
questions: Walk me through your three biggest expense lines. Are they where you would expect them to be?
What has grown fastest over the last two years, and why?
What is in here that no longer earns its place?
Which of these could flex if revenue dropped?

agenda.title: Invoicing process review
agenda.detail: Review how and when invoices are raised, and where cash is being delayed by process rather than by customers. Late invoicing is one of the most common and most fixable cash constraints in an SME.
questions: How quickly after the work is done does the invoice go out?
Who raises invoices, and is it their priority or the last thing on their list?
What are your payment terms, and are they actually enforced?
How long are customers really taking to pay?
Who follows up overdue accounts?
How often does an invoice get queried or corrected?

agenda.title: Margin leaks and cost structure
agenda.detail: Identify low-margin offerings, delivery inefficiency and rework, overuse of subcontractors or casuals, operational waste, structural cost issues. Help the owner choose a small number of high-impact changes, not an overwhelming list.

agenda.title: Financial rhythm and reporting
agenda.detail: Define the cadence: weekly or fortnightly metric check, monthly financial review, quarterly accountant engagement. Confirm who produces the numbers and who reviews them. Keep it light enough that the owner will sustain it.

agenda.title: Close and link forward
agenda.detail: Show how financial improvement funds hiring, supports systems work, and strengthens enterprise value. Name the next module in this client's sequence.

items: Finalise the Financial Health Summary and the Margin & Cost Improvement Plan.
Document the invoicing changes agreed, with a named owner and a start date.
Confirm the reporting rhythm and the metrics to be tracked.
Note any financial constraint that will affect later modules, particularly V2 Strategy, V4 People hiring capacity, and V6 Technology spend.

must_not: redo bookkeeping or rebuild the accounts
build detailed three-way forecasts
provide tax, BAS or compliance advice
configure accounting or invoicing software directly; the advisor designs the process, the client or their bookkeeper makes the system change
promise specific profit outcomes
guardrails.note: These are boundaries of profession, not boundaries of module. Where V1 surfaces an issue whose home module is elsewhere, the advisor addresses it and records the output against that module.

quality_standards: The owner can explain their financial position in their own words.
Expense and margin actions are few, specific and realistic.
Invoicing changes are practical and have a named owner.
A reporting rhythm exists and has a named owner.

title: Strategy & Planning
focus: Direction for the next one to five years, captured in a workshop and written up as a strategic business plan the owner owns.
purpose: V2 is where the owner stops reacting and starts leading. A facilitated workshop works through the Strategy Workbook to capture direction, business model, competitive position and priorities. Trinity then drafts the Strategic Business Plan from those inputs, the advisor walks the client through it, and the client takes it away to adjust and make their own.
core_outcomes: A completed Strategy Workbook capturing the client's strategic inputs.
A written Strategic Business Plan is created.
The owner can state where the business is going, and why, in their own words.
The owner has the plan in hand, understands it, and knows what they want to change.

notes.text: Upload is optional but strongly recommended. The more source material Trinity receives, the more of the workbook it pre-fills, and the less workshop time is spent on data entry rather than strategy.
The plan template already covers priorities, key actions and positioning, so no separate priorities map or value proposition document is produced.
Both tools already exist in Trinity. V2 requires no new tool build and should not draw on the Feature 3 allocation.

required_inputs.label: Diagnostic report and advisor recommendations
Owner's stated goals, growth constraint and "fix one thing" response
SWOT, competitor and industry responses from the diagnostic
Previous strategic plans or business plans
Organisational chart
Product and service documentation
Financial reports: P&L, budgets, forecasts
Competitor list or analysis
Marketing material
Outputs from any completed module
required_inputs.fallback: V2 does not assume any other module has run. It may be the first module a client starts with. Where V1 is complete, its financial outputs sharpen the session. Where it is not, the client's own financial reports serve the same purpose.

preparation_checklist.text: Gather all available source material from the client and from Trinity.

Run the Strategy Workbook generator. Trinity extracts vision, mission, values, goals, products and services, structure, competitors, financials, SWOT indicators, market segments, customer behaviour, growth opportunities and past initiatives, then produces a pre-filled workbook.
Review the pre-filled workbook. Correct anything Trinity has misread and note the gaps that need the client to fill them.
Read the owner's free-text diagnostic responses closely. Their own language should carry into the plan.
Note where the diagnostic or the financials disagree with the owner's stated ambition. That gap is the session's most useful material.

sessions.title: Strategy Workshop
sessions.note: The pre-filled Strategy Workbook is the capture tool for the session. Where two advisors are available, the lead facilitates and whiteboards while the second types summaries into the workbook and photographs each whiteboard before it is erased.

agenda.title: Frame the session
agenda.detail: Explain that this session sets direction, not operational detail, and that the workbook captures everything for the plan that follows.

agenda.title: Review the pre-filled workbook
agenda.detail: Walk the client through what Trinity has already extracted. Confirm, correct, and identify what is missing. This sets the pace and shows the client the work already done.

agenda.title: Vision, values and goals
agenda.detail: Vision, mission and values. Business goals and personal goals, kept distinct. Where the owner wants the business to be, and what they want their own life to look like alongside it.
questions: Where do you want this business to be in three years?
What does that look like on an ordinary Tuesday?
What do you want out of it personally?
What are you not willing to give up to get there?

agenda.title: Business model, products and customers
agenda.detail: Products and services, divisions and structure, market segments, customer needs, trends and buying behaviour. What the business actually sells, to whom, and what genuinely drives revenue.
questions: Which customers do you want more of?
What do they actually buy, and why from you?
Where does the money really come from, and is that where your time goes?

agenda.title: Competitive position and SWOT
agenda.detail: Competitors, competitive advantage, barriers to entry, and the full SWOT. Test the owner's assessment rather than accepting it. Test in both directions. Owners routinely overclaim the soft advantages and underclaim the durable ones. "Great service" is not an advantage, it is table stakes and every competitor claims it. The advantages that genuinely hold in an SME are unglamorous: location, switching costs, an accumulated customer database, long relationships, a specific accreditation or licence, exclusive supply, or simply being the one everybody already knows. Where an owner rates the business as easy to replicate, check whether that is actually true before agreeing with them.
questions: Could a competitor copy this within twelve months if they spent money on it?
Would a customer notice if it disappeared?
Does it change what someone pays or who they choose?

agenda.title: Growth opportunities and priorities
agenda.detail: Growth opportunities, past initiatives and what happened to them, and the priorities for the next twelve months. Push toward a focused set rather than a wishlist.

agenda.title: Close
agenda.detail: Confirm the workbook is complete enough. Explain that the plan will be drafted and presented at the next meeting.

agenda.title: Purpose
agenda.detail: This session is to walk the client through the drafted plan, not to rewrite it live.

agenda.title: Walk the plan
agenda.detail: Section by section, in plain language. Check the owner recognises their own business and their own words in it.

agenda.title: Priorities and 90-day actions
agenda.detail: Confirm the twelve-month priorities and the first ninety days of action, with owners against each.

agenda.title: Handover
agenda.detail: Hand the plan to the client to review, adjust and make their own. Agree a date for the adjusted version to come back.

items: Run the Strategic Business Plan generator, uploading the completed workbook, whiteboard photographs and any supporting documents.
Generate the One-Page Summary where the client will use it.
Read the plan in full before the walkthrough.
Issue the plan and the one-pager to the client.
Confirm the date the client will return their adjusted version.
Note any priority that will require work in a later module, so it is not lost when that module opens.

must_not: write the plan by hand rather than through the tool
complete the workbook on the client's behalf; the content must be the client's
produce detailed market research or industry analysis
drift into operational or project planning
forecast or promise the financial outcome of a strategic option
rewrite the plan live during the walkthrough
guardrails.note: These are boundaries of profession, not boundaries of module. Where V2 surfaces an issue whose home module is elsewhere, the advisor addresses it and records the output against that module.

quality_standards: The workbook is complete enough that the plan can be drafted without going back to the client.
The plan reads as the owner's business, in the owner's language.
The owner can state the direction of the business in a sentence or two without reading it back.
Twelve-month priorities are focused, with a named owner against each.
The client returns an adjusted plan rather than filing it untouched.

title: Leadership & Communications
focus: How leaders behave, who decides what, and how information moves.
purpose: V3 defines how the business is led day to day: what leaders are expected to do, who holds which decisions, how information travels up, down and out, and what rhythm holds it all together. Strategy and structure both fail without this. It is a light module in advisor effort and consistently high in value.
core_outcomes: Leadership behaviours and expectations are defined and written down.
Decision rights are clear: who decides what, and what escalates.
Communication pathways are mapped in both directions.
A meeting rhythm exists, with agendas and a named owner for each meeting.

notes.title: Where there is no leadership layer
notes.text: Many clients have no managers. The module still runs. Leadership expectations become the owner's own operating standard, decision rights identify what could be delegated and to whom, and the rhythm may be a single weekly team meeting. Where the business needs a leadership layer it does not yet have, that becomes an input to V4 and V9 rather than something invented in this session.
No Trinity use during the live session.
No optional deliverables. The Playbook is explicit that this module stays at three outputs, with no additional frameworks.

required_inputs.label: Diagnostic report, V3 module assessment
Diagnostic responses on management meetings, team meetings and director alignment
Owner's stated goals and "fix one thing" response
V2 Strategic Business Plan and priorities
required_inputs.fallback: Where V2 has not run, the owner's stated goals from the diagnostic serve in place of the strategic priorities.

required_inputs.label: List of people in leadership or supervisory roles, or confirmation there are none
Existing meeting agendas or terms of reference

preparation_checklist.text: Review the diagnostic responses on meeting rhythms, management and team meetings, and director alignment.
Where V2 is complete, review the strategic priorities. Leadership behaviour should be defined against what the strategy actually requires.
Establish who is genuinely in a leadership role. This often does not match job titles.
Identify the recurring patterns to test in the session: inconsistent communication, unclear decision-making, reactive leadership, the owner as bottleneck.
Prepare discussion notes: questions to ask, areas to clarify, and specific examples observed in earlier work.

agenda.title: Frame the session
agenda.detail: Explain that strategy and structure both fail without aligned leadership, and that this session defines how leaders behave, decide and communicate.

agenda.title: Leadership expectations
agenda.detail: Define what leaders must consistently do, and what staff should be able to expect from them.
questions: What behaviours must leaders here consistently demonstrate?
What should any staff member be able to expect from a leader?
Where do leaders currently undermine each other, even unintentionally?
How should the direction of the business be presented to teams?

agenda.title: Decision rights
agenda.detail: Establish who decides what, at what threshold, and what must escalate. This is where owner bottlenecks are named and removed.
questions: What decisions come to you that should not?
What is the largest decision someone else can make without asking you?
What are you afraid will happen if you let go of that?
What must always come to you, and why?
agenda.note: Record simply: decision, decider, threshold, escalates to.

agenda.title: Communication pathways
agenda.detail: Map how information moves down, up and out. What escalates, how staff raise issues, how leaders update teams, and who speaks externally.

agenda.title: Meeting rhythm
agenda.detail: Confirm the cadence and scale it to the size of the business. Typically a weekly huddle, a monthly management meeting and a quarterly strategy review. Confirm who runs each, who attends, and the standing agenda.

agenda.title: Close
agenda.detail: Confirm what changes on Monday.

items: Finalise the three documents and issue them to the client.
Confirm the first date each meeting in the new cadence will run, and who owns it.
Where a decision right has moved away from the owner, note it as evidence for V9.

must_not: coach individuals
mediate conflict between people
address individual performance issues
draft or rewrite HR policy
run the client's meetings on their behalf
guardrails.note: This module is alignment-focused, not HR or coaching. These are boundaries of profession, not boundaries of module. Where V3 surfaces an issue whose home module is elsewhere, the advisor addresses it and records the output against that module.

quality_standards: Leadership expectations are in plain language and specific enough to act on.
Decision rights name a person, not a role the business does not have.
At least one decision has moved away from the owner.
The meeting rhythm is scaled to the business, with a named owner for each meeting.
Nothing in the outputs assumes a leadership layer the business does not have.

title: People & Structure
focus: The right people in the right roles, with clear accountability, and a structure that matches where the business is going.
purpose:
V4 aligns team, roles, structure and capability with the direction of the business. The focus is clarity and accountability: who does what, which tasks should move, where the gaps are, and what the owner is still carrying that someone else should.

The module runs whether or not the business has an HR function, a leadership team, or more than a handful of staff. Where it surfaces a need for leadership development, HR support or recruitment, those needs are real and important. They are referred to the Talent team rather than delivered inside this module.
core_outcomes: Current and intended structure are documented and the difference between them is understood.
Every key role has clear responsibilities, with each task tested for retain, lose or gain.
Capability gaps are identified, with a decision on build, hire or outsource for each.
Key person and retention risks are named, with a view on whether each is addressable.
Position descriptions exist, or the client can produce them.

notes.title: Where the team is very small
notes.text: Many clients have two or three staff, or none. The module still runs. Structure becomes who does what and what the owner is still holding personally. Role clarity may cover two roles. Capability gaps often point at the owner rather than the team. Where the finding is that the business needs people it cannot currently afford, that belongs in V1 and V2 rather than being solved here.

Before the session the pack generator asks whether existing position descriptions are available. Where they are, the advisor loads them, and the tool examines them and pre-fills the roles and responsibilities matrix ready for the workshop. After the session it produces the deliverables. The Position Description generator is also made available to the client directly.

D2 and D3 both come out of the single role clarity activity, which also informs the intended structure in D1. The advisor produces the first two position descriptions as worked examples, and the client generates the remainder in Trinity, so module completion does not wait on the client.

notes.title: Referral to the Talent team
notes.text: People issues are not out of scope for this module and must not be avoided. Leadership development, HR support and recruitment are services BBA delivers through the Talent team. Where the module surfaces a need in any of these areas, the advisor names it, records it, and refers the client, rather than either delivering it here or leaving it unaddressed. Employment law matters are handled case by case.

required_inputs.label: Diagnostic report, V4 module assessment
Diagnostic HR responses: headcount, contracts, policies, position descriptions, retention and recruitment flags
V2 Strategic Business Plan and priorities
required_inputs.fallback: Where V2 has not run, the owner's stated goals from the diagnostic serve in place of the strategic priorities.

required_inputs.label: V3 Leadership Alignment Summary and decision rights
required_inputs.fallback: Where V3 has not run, decision rights are established here at role level only.

required_inputs.label: Current team list with roles and reporting lines
Existing position descriptions
Existing organisational chart

preparation_checklist.text: Review the diagnostic HR responses, particularly the retention and recruitment flags, policy gaps and contract status.
Draft the current structure from the team list and any existing organisational chart.

Run the pack generator. Where the client has existing position descriptions, load them so the tool can pre-fill the roles and responsibilities matrix, and session time goes on testing tasks rather than listing them.
Identify structural issues to test: overlapping responsibilities, gaps with no owner, unclear reporting lines, and work the owner is doing that someone else should.
Where V2 is complete, review the strategic priorities. The intended structure should be the one that delivers them.

agenda.title: Frame the session
agenda.detail: Explain that this session is about roles and structure, not individual performance, and that no one will be assessed personally.

agenda.title: Current structure review
agenda.detail: Walk the draft structure. Confirm who actually does what, as opposed to what the chart says. Identify overlaps, gaps, unclear reporting and work sitting with the owner.
questions: Who actually decides here?
What falls between two people?
What has no owner at all?
What are you doing that someone on this list should be doing?

agenda.title: Retention and key person risk
agenda.detail: Identify who the business cannot afford to lose, and who is at risk of leaving. Establish whether each risk is addressable and how quickly. Held before the role work, because a departure changes what can be planned.
questions: If one person resigned tomorrow, who would hurt most, and why?
Is anyone unsettled right now? What is driving that, and is it something you can act on?
What would we lose that only exists in that person's head?

agenda.title: Roles, responsibilities and task review
agenda.detail:
The core activity of the module. Work role by role. For each role, list the actual tasks, then test every task against three options.

Run across every role, this single activity delivers structure, role clarity, capability and gaps in one pass. Tasks with no home expose structural gaps. Tasks nobody can do expose capability gaps. Tasks the owner cannot put down expose the dependency V9 addresses.

Start with the owner's own role. It is usually the most overloaded, and doing it first sets the tone for honest answers about everyone else.

options.definition: stays with this role and is being done well enough
should move off this role, to another role, to a system, to an outsourced provider, or stopped entirely
should be picked up by this role, whether it currently sits with the owner, sits nowhere, or is not being done at all

questions: What does this person actually spend their week on?
Which of these can only they do?
What is on this list because they have always done it?
What is being done twice?
What is on nobody's list?
agenda.note: Record against each role: responsibilities retained, tasks moving off, tasks moving on, decision rights, reporting line, and any capability gap the changes create.

agenda.title: Close
agenda.detail: Confirm the first change and who owns it.

deliverables.title: Role Clarity Map, with task retain, lose and gain

items: Finalise the structure pack and issue it to the client.
Generate the first two position descriptions as worked examples, then show the client how to produce the rest.
Refer any leadership development, HR or recruitment need to the Talent team, and record the referral.
Record key person risks as evidence for V9.
Note any capability gap with a cost implication, so it carries into the financial and strategic work rather than being agreed in isolation.

must_not: conduct performance management or assess individuals
become involved in disciplinary matters
provide employment law advice, or draft contracts, policies or workplace agreements
benchmark salaries, unless separately engaged to do so
deliver leadership development, HR or recruitment services inside this module
guardrails.note: These are boundaries of profession, not boundaries of module. Where V4 surfaces an issue whose home module is elsewhere, the advisor addresses it and records the output against that module.

quality_standards: Every key role has been through retain, lose and gain against its actual tasks, starting with the owner's.
At least one task has moved off the owner's role.
The intended structure is achievable rather than aspirational, and the owner can say what changes first.
Capability gaps carry a decision, not just a description.
Key person risks are named, each with a stated position on whether it can be addressed.
Any leadership, HR or recruitment need has been referred to the Talent team and recorded.

title: Systems & Processes
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Document and improve the systems and processes that keep the business running.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: List the business's core operating processes

title: Technology
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Assess the business's technology stack and identify improvement opportunities.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: List the current technology stack

title: Sales & Marketing
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Sharpen the business's sales and marketing engine.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: Review current sales pipeline and marketing channels

title: Brand, IP & Protection
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Clarify what makes the business defensible and differentiated.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: List brand and IP assets

title: Owner Independence
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Reduce owner dependency so the business can run without the owner in the room.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: List tasks only the owner currently does

title: Value & Growth
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Focus on the retention, concentration, and recurring-revenue drivers of business value and growth.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: Review customer concentration and revenue quality

title: Risk, Legal, Compliance & Property
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Identify and reduce legal, compliance, and property-related risk.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: Review key contracts, leases, and compliance obligations

title: Re-Diagnostic Capstone
purpose: PLACEHOLDER: Re-run the diagnostic, see the value movement since the last one, and get routed back through the module library with a refreshed focus.

preparation_checklist.text: PLACEHOLDER: Review progress made across the modules since the last diagnostic
